review_hold.body: 正式な学名記載はまだない（暫定名）。Fort Sherman は Panama の Canal Zone（Colón県）にある旧米軍基地名に由来し、1980年代に植物収集家 Jay Vannini が現地で採集した papillilaminum 型個体群のクローン名として流布した。園芸界では単独のクローン名（FS）として流通し、'Ralph Lynam' など他の canal-type paps と交配される例が多い。インドネシア系の流通株と「同名だが別系統」との混同が見られ、文献・商業情報の一致度は高いが系統同定には注意が必要（主な出典：Jay Vannini 記述系記事、Croat の Panama リビジョン）。
review_hold.body_en: Formal botanical publication of "Anthurium 'Fort Sherman'" does not exist; the name is a horticultural/collector epithet. The label refers to a dark papillilaminum clone collected by plantsman Jay Vannini in the 1980s near the U.S. Army base Fort Sherman in the Panama Canal/Colón area. In cultivation it is treated as a named canal‑ecotype clone of Anthurium papillilaminum (abbreviated FS) and figures widely as a parent in hybrids (e.g. FS × RL). Commercial growers and reseller listings commonly use the name, though Indonesian trade plants of similar appearance are sometimes sold under the same name despite uncertain shared origin. Primary support comes from Vannini’s horticultural accounts and Croat’s Panama treatment noting Fort Sherman as a locality.

review_hold.body: Anthurium radicans は 1854 年、K.Koch & Haage が Index Seminum [Berlin] 10 で記載した。分布はブラジル。種小名はラテン語で「rooting」を意味する。Anthurium radicansは欧州の栽培材料から記載され、Kew標本K000501777が近年ネオタイプとして指定された（Pimenta et al., 2025）。野生産地の同定は後年の採集と研究で明確化された。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium radicans was described by K.Koch & Haage in 1854 in Index Seminum [Berlin] 10. Distribution: Brazil. The epithet radicans derives from Latin meaning 'rooting.' Anthurium radicans was described from cultivated garden material and lacked a precise protologue locality; recent typification designated a neotype (K barcode K000501777) at Kew. Taxonomic clarification and conservation assessment were published by Pimenta et al. (Willdenowia, 2025).

review_hold.body: Anthurium vittariifolium は 1905 年、Engl. が Pflanzenr. 4, Fam. 23b: 88 で記載した。分布はブラジル、コロンビア、エクアドル、ペルー。種小名はVittaria属の葉に似ることに由来する。タイプ標本はUle 5624（Brazil, Amazonas, upper Rio Juruá、1901年採集）とされ、Engl.が1905年に記載した。命名・タイプ照合はDelannay & Croat (2020) および POWO に記載あり。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium vittariifolium was described by Engl. in 1905 in Pflanzenr. 4, Fam. 23b: 88. Distribution: Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru. The epithet vittariifolium means 'with leaves like Vittaria' (fern). The type is cited as Ule 5624 collected in Brazil (Amazonas, upper Rio Juruá) in July 1901; Engler published the name in 1905. Nomenclatural and type citations appear in Delannay & Croat (2020) and Plants of the World Online.

review_hold.body: Anthurium queremalense は Croat が記載した。種小名はQueremal（Valle del Cauca, Colombia）に由来すると推定される。T. B. Croat によるQueremal付近（26 July 1997）の採集記録が確認されるが、正式なプロトローグやIPNI/POWO登録が見当たらないため命名学的地位は未確定。出典はCroat et al. (Aroideana)およびJBB標本記録。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium queremalense was described by Croat. The epithet appears to refer to Queremal (Valle del Cauca, Colombia). T. B. Croat collected Anthurium material near Queremal (26 July 1997) as cited in Croat et al. (Aroideana), and the name is used in some herbarium records (JBB). No formal protologue or IPNI/POWO entry was found, so the nomenclatural status is uncertain.

B. Croat（1996 年採集）。分布はボリビア。種小名はLibby Besseに因み命名された。原料はLibby Besseが1986-01-25にBolivia, Cochabamba（Chapare, near Villa Tunari）で採集した生株で、Selby Botanical Gardensで栽培・開花し、T. B. Croatが1996-09-29に標本化した（Croat 2005）。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium besseae was described by Croat in 2005 in Novon 15(1): 84 (-85; fig. 2B-C). Type locality: Cochabamba: Chapare, old road. from Cochabamba to Villa Tunari, vic. Villa Tunari, alt. 240 m. Collected by T. B. Croat (1996). Distribution: Bolivia. Epithet honors Libby Besse. Croat (2005) states the living plant was originally collected by Libby Besse on 25 January 1986 near Villa Tunari, Cochabamba, Bolivia; it flowered in cultivation at Selby Botanical Gardens and T. B. Croat designated the type from that cultivated plant on 29 September 1996. No additional nomenclatural notes are given in the protologue.

No additional published etymology or introduction-to-cultivation account was found in the cited protologue.

The epithet marmoratum is interpreted as Latin for 'marbled'. Anthurium marmoratum was described by Luis Sodiro in 1903 (Anales Univ. Centr. Ecuador). The protologue/type information cites Ecuador, Pichincha — along Rio Toachi and Rio Pilon (Sodiro s.n.). There are no widely recorded major nomenclatural changes for this name.

Ecuador (1902) に記載された学名であり、POWO と IPNI では本名を受容し複数の異名（例: Anthurium angamarcanum など）を列挙している。原標本の採集者情報や確定的な採集地は該当データベースで確認できなかった。

Anthurium dolichostachyum was described by Luis Sodiro in Anales Univ. Centr. Ecuador (1902). POWO and IPNI treat the name as accepted and list several heterotypic synonyms (e.g. Anthurium angamarcanum). review_hold.body: Anthurium portillae は Croat が記載した。種小名はPortilla（Pepe Portilla）に献名されたと推測されるが、Anthurium portillae は有効出版されていない園芸名（nom. nud.）として流通しており、Anthurium papillilaminum や A. sizemoreae と混同される事例が報告されている。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium portillae was described by Croat. The epithet appears to honor Portilla (Pepe Portilla). Anthurium portillae is widely used in cultivation as an unpublished horticultural name (nomen nudum) and is not accepted as a validly published species in major taxonomic databases; it has frequently been confused with Anthurium papillilaminum and material related to A. sizemoreae.

review_hold.body_en: Anthurium faustomirandae was described by Pérez-Farr. & Croat in 2001 in Novon 11(1): 88 (-91; figs. 1-2). Collected by M.A.Pérez-Farrera. Distribution: Mexico. The epithet honors botanist Faustino Miranda, noted for his work in Chiapas and association with the Jardin Botanico Faustino Miranda. Anthurium faustomirandae was formally described by Pérez-Farrera & Croat in Novon (2001). No published synonyms or nomenclatural recombinations have been recorded in major checklists.

review_hold.body: Anthurium metallicum は 1860 年、Linden ex Schott が Prodr. Syst. Aroid. 506 で記載した。分布はコロンビア。種小名 metallicum は金属のような光沢を指す。名称は Linden 提案を Schott が1860年に出版して成立した。Schott の記載材料は栽培個体に基づき野生産地が不確かとされ、2005年に Jacome & Croat により Colombia で再発見・再記載された。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium metallicum was described by Linden ex Schott in 1860 in Prodr. Syst. Aroid. 506. Distribution: Colombia. The epithet metallicum (Latin: 'metallic') refers to a metallic sheen. The name was proposed by Linden and validly published by H. W. Schott (1860). Schott's description appears based on cultivated material of uncertain wild origin; Jacome & Croat (2005) redescribed the taxon and reported its rediscovery in Colombia.

review_hold.body: Anthurium hookeri は 1841 年、Kunth が Enum. Pl. 3: 74 で記載した。分布はフランス領ギアナ、ガイアナ、Netherlands Antilles、スリナム、Trinidad-Tobago、ベネズエラ、Venezuelan Antilles、Windward Is.。Kunthが1841年に記載し、Mayo(1982)がSchott drawing 517をレクトタイプに指定した。栽培界では名前の濫用が多く、Anthurium amplum や A. huegelii などが同義語扱いされることがある。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium hookeri was described by Kunth in 1841 in Enum. Pl. 3: 74. Distribution: French Guiana, Guyana, Netherlands Antilles, Suriname, Trinidad-Tobago, Venezuela, Venezuelan Antilles, Windward Is.. Described by Kunth in 1841. Simon J. Mayo (1982) designated Schott drawing 517 as the lectotype. The name Anthurium hookeri has been widely misapplied in cultivation. POWO/IPNI record several synonyms (e.g., Anthurium amplum, A. huegelii, A. neglectum) and a forma longicuneatum (Engl.).

review_hold.body: 正式な学名記載はまだない（未記載種／暫定名）。「Anthurium sp. 'BVIT'」は園芸通称で、Black Velvet Indo Type（BVIT）の略。Indo（インドネシア）で育種・選抜されたダークな“velvet”系のアンスリウム群を指す園芸タグで、単一クローンではなく複数の系統・品種がこのタグで流通している。多くのインドネシアナーセリーや輸出業者が流通源であり、親植物や野外の標本は公表されていない。形質的にはしばしば papillilaminum 類似とされるが、正式な学術記載・タイプ情報は見つかっていない（出典は園芸情報と専門ガイド）。
review_hold.body_en: Anthurium sp. 'BVIT' is not a published species name but a horticultural trade tag: "Black Velvet Indo Type" (BVIT). Community and nursery sources explain BVIT as an informal label used for dark, velvet-surfaced Anthurium seedlings and clones originating from Indonesian breeding and selection programs rather than a single described taxon. It commonly appears in nursery catalogs and hybrid pedigrees (used as a parent in many crosses), and is repeatedly described as papillilaminum-like in appearance. No formal protologue, IPNI/POWO/Tropicos entry, or herbarium type has been located; parentage and original collector are not documented in the literature. Sources agree on trade-origin and Indonesian provenance, but differ or are silent about any single breeder or precise wild origin.
